study type: secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: length of time for dilation from 4 to 6 cm
outcome: maternal morbidity (postpartum fever, wound infection, hemorrhage)
neonatal morbidity (neonatal death, hypothermic therapy, mechanical ventilation, respiratory distress, meconium aspiration syndrome, seizure, or treatment of sepsis)
cohort: 7355 patients at ≥37 weeks presenting in spontaneous or induced labor with a nonanomalous living singleton in vertex presentation
finding: Patients whose dilation time from 4 to 6 cm exceeded the 90th percentile (10.3 hours) had increased odds of cesarean delivery, maternal morbidity, and neonatal morbidity.
